business: Bonita Style Houston, a modest-fashion boutique (thobes, kaftans, abayas, jalabiyas, bishts)
by_segment: South Asian Muslim woman (Pakistani, Indian or Bangladeshi family)
East African or African-American Muslim woman
Arab-American woman (Levantine, Gulf, Egyptian, Iraqi or Maghrebi family)
Modest dresser who is not part of a big local community (convert, Latina or Christian modest dresser)
why_not: I like that I can try things on, and Westheimer isn't far from where I shop on Hillcroft, so I might stop in and look. But there is no Eid or wedding on my calendar in November, and I already have abayas and hijabs at home, so I would most likely walk out without buying.

I shop when there's an occasion coming, and in early November there's no Eid or Ramadan on my calendar. I'm not driving up to Westchase for 15% off things I don't need yet. I'd save the TikTok and look again before Ramadan.

I get my abayas for $20 to $30 on Amazon or TikTok Shop and wait for sales, so $45 for an everyday one, or $75 to $80 for a thobe, is more than I usually pay, even with 15% off. Driving out to Westchase on a Sunday to look at racks that might not be my style isn't worth it for me.

Eid is months away and I don't have a wedding coming up, so I can't justify $75 to $80 for a thobe when I can get an abaya for $25 online. I might save the videos and maybe stop by later, but I'm not driving up Southwest Freeway on a Sunday just to browse.

I already have an aunty's boutique near Hillcroft and a bazaar seller in Sugar Land who know my size and my family. I don't need to drive out to Westheimer for a 15% off opening day when nothing big like Eid is coming up this month.

My sister in Karachi and my cousins in Dubai send me pieces, and I stock up when I travel, where an embroidered thobe costs me a fraction of $75. Westchase is close enough off the freeway that I might look on a weekend, but nothing is pulling me there in November with no Eid or wedding coming.

A brand-new store has zero Google Maps reviews on opening day, and I don't try a place until I've read what other women say about the fit, the fabric and the staff. There's no Eid or wedding coming up for me this month either, so nothing is pushing me to go in early for 15% off.

A store that opens on November 1 has no Google Maps reviews yet, and I don't drive out to Westheimer for a place nobody I know has tried. I'll wait to see what people say about the fabric and the stitching first.

Thobes, jalabiyas and bishts are Gulf-style. For Eid and weddings I wear shalwar kameez and desi suits with colour and embroidery, so nothing on that list is what I actually shop for. I might grab a $10 chiffon hijab if I'm passing by after jummah, but I wouldn't go out of my way on opening day for that.
why_yes: A store near Westchase with fitting rooms and staff who help with length is exactly what I want, and it's a short drive from where I already shop on weekends. If the crepe feels solid when I touch it, I'd pick up one thobe or abaya for upcoming weddings, but I won't fill a bag on the first visit.

Westchase is right by Hillcroft where I already go on weekends, and being able to try on and get the length checked fixes my main problem with ordering online. I'd stop in, probably grab an everyday abaya and a couple of hijabs with the 15% off, but I'm not dropping $120 on a jalabiya set with no Eid coming up.
flip: If my friends showed up in Bonita thobes at a wedding or henna night and the embroidery looked better than what my usual shop carries, I'd make the drive to see it.
Seeing the embroidered thobes in person and finding the crepe heavy and well finished, with lengths that fit me without hemming, especially if a family wedding comes up.
Seeing pieces in colors and cuts that fit my taste, at a real sale price on the everyday abayas (around $30), would get me to stop by.
A wedding or henna night on my calendar in the next few weeks, plus seeing that the pieces are modern and dressy, not just basic abayas.
A Live or video showing the fabric and stitching up close next to a cheap online abaya, plus a deal on an everyday abaya and hijab together, or a family event coming up that I need an outfit for.
A wedding or event coming up soon, or the same kind of discount and fitting help running in the weeks before Ramadan.
Seeing a TikTok or Live from them with colourful embroidered pieces or kaftans styled the way desi aunties dress for Eid and dholkis, at under $60.
If I had a wedding or Eid coming up and they had pieces in a proper long length that I could try on and take home the same day, with the 15% off still going.
Touching the fabric and finding it heavy, opaque and soft, with proper embroidery, right before a family wedding or Eid when I don't have time to get something sent from home.

A real sale I can't get online, like everyday abayas around $30 or a buy-two deal, plus seeing in person that the fabric is thick and not scratchy. I'd maybe go closer to Eid or a wedding when I need something nicer anyway.
A few months of solid Google Maps reviews with customer photos showing modern, less traditional cuts, or a friend from the masjid wearing something from there that I actually like.
If they did a TikTok Live showing the embroidery and crepe up close next to a cheap online abaya, with a real deal on the $45 everyday abaya I could order without driving across town.
A wedding or henna invite in the next few weeks, plus seeing a statement piece in the store that I can't find at the Hillcroft shops.

A last-minute need I can't wait on family for, like a wedding or henna night outfit I need in a specific size this week, and seeing in person that the embroidery and fabric are better quality than what I get back home.
If a friend or my cousin showed me a thobe from there that was clearly better quality than what my shop carries, or if they had something specific I couldn't find for an upcoming wedding.
Seeing TikTok videos of colorful, trendy pieces that actually look like my style, with everyday abayas around $30 or a real clearance or sale rack.
A few months of solid Google reviews with real photos, or a friend from the Hillcroft markets wearing one of their thobes to a wedding and it looking well made.
